_comment: Finding-level adjudication of run-1 on mt-test-studio @ 36972b38 (post-fix code, 2026-08-27).
STANDARD, taken from the earlier adjudication of run-4: two questions per finding, not one.
2. Would the proposed code actually run, and in the direction claimed?
The second question is what overturned verdicts last time and it overturned four here.
adjudicated:false — this is ONE model pass. The prior adjudication's own note applies:
'two model passes agreeing is not a human confirming.' A single pass is weaker still.
Every 'wrong' verdict below states a checkable reason so a human can overturn it cheaply.
HEADLINE: 29 right, 4 wrong, 2 duplicate, 8 questionable of 43 published.
Precision 67% (29/43) against a 70% gate — just short, and far above the 14% defect-truth
floor, which was never a precision figure.
VOCABULARY matches the run-4 adjudication (real / real-cold / wrong / marginal) so bench/score.mjs
reads it without a second dialect. Duplicates are scored `marginal`, not `real`: the finding is
correct but redundant, and counting it in the numerator would inflate precision.
adjudicatedBy: one model pass; pending human confirmation

verdicts.title: Use an indexed existence probe for duplicate runs
verdicts.why: The proposal is `.only("pk").exists()` where the original is `.exists()`. `.only()` controls which columns are SELECTed when model instances are materialised; `.exists()` materialises nothing — it compiles to `SELECT (1) AS a1 ... LIMIT 1` and ignores deferred-field state entirely. The two statements emit identical SQL. This is a no-op published at `high` with two counted facts and grounding `verified`, which makes it the single worst finding in the run.
verdicts.gateShouldHaveCaught: no-op — but the rule compares collapsed whitespace, and these differ textually.

verdicts.title: Materialize only the needed plan keys
verdicts.why: A real redundant or per-iteration query; the proposed rewrite is valid Django and reduces round trips or columns in the direction claimed.

verdicts.title: Stream the matching users through the queryset
verdicts.why: `.iterator()` reduces peak memory; it does not reduce queries, and the finding is categorised `full-scan` with zero counted facts. It is also risky in this specific loop: `deactivate` writes inside the iteration, and a server-side cursor held open across writes is a different operational profile. Real observation, wrong category, unproven benefit.

verdicts.title: Materialize plan ids before filtering plans
verdicts.why: VERIFIED AGAINST SOURCE (forms.py:364-367). `plan_ids` is a lazy queryset, so Django compiles `pk__in=plan_ids` into a subquery — one round trip. The proposal wraps it in `list(...)`, which forces a separate evaluation and passes literal ids: two round trips where there was one. Classified `equivalent`, which it is; it is simply slower.
verdicts.gateShouldHaveCaught: wrong-direction. It did not, because readOrmShape counts 0 evaluating calls on both sides — `list(qs)` is not counted as a round trip — so the 0-vs-0 guard added this session lets it through. See the note on that guard below.

whatThisExposed: THE 0-VS-0 GUARD HAS A COST. Narrowing wrong-direction to require a count to compare was right in principle — one of the five findings it previously suppressed was a genuine improvement — but finding #5 is a genuine wrong-direction that it now lets through. The trade was not free. The real fix is upstream: readOrmShape does not count `list(queryset)` as an evaluating call, so a rewrite that adds one reads as 0-vs-0. It already detects `list(` for its `materialised` flag; the count should use it.

THREE OF FOUR FALSE POSITIVES ARE NO-OPS THE GATE COULD NOT SEE. #1 (.only on .exists), #27 (self-declared identical) and #31 (parenthesis removal) all emit identical SQL. The no-op rule compares collapsed whitespace, which catches formatting but not semantic identity. A no-op rule that understood `.only()` has no effect on `.exists()`, and that normalised redundant parentheses, would have removed three of the four.
SEVERITY IS NOT THE PROBLEM. The four wrong findings sit at high/medium/low/low, and the 29 right ones span the same range. Reading only the `high` band would still have surfaced #1.

postFixGateReplay._what: The CURRENT value gate replayed over run-1's own findings. The gate is deterministic and takes no model call, so this is a measurement of the gate change, not a projection of a future run. It is the same technique bench/fixtures/mt-test-studio-2026-08-26.json uses in the test suite.
postFixGateReplay._caveat: Replayed with an empty file map, so vocabulary-dependent rules (invented-symbol) abstain. That makes the replay conservative — it can only under-suppress relative to a real run. None of run-1's 43 published findings were invented-symbol suppressions, so the published set replays faithfully.

suppressedByNewGate.note: .only() is inert before .exists() — the semantic no-op rule.
list(queryset) now counts as a round trip, so the gate has 0-vs-1 to compare.
redundant parentheses, via the balanced-paren normaliser.
the duplicate of #28; list(union) is now counted.

remainingWrong.why: An excerpt-boundary artefact, not a semantic no-op: the proposal wraps the original queryset in a `for` header, and the enclosing loop was outside the excerpt. The no-op rule was deliberately NOT widened to catch it — that would mean treating an added statement as no change, which is false in general. Fixing it belongs in excerpt selection, not in the gate.

postFixGateReplay._verdict: Precision 74% (29/39) against a 70% gate — over, from 67%. Three of the four adjudicated false positives are gone, and no finding verdicted `real` or `real-cold` was suppressed. Confirming this end-to-end needs a fresh scan; the gate half is measured.
